ranked_evidence.title: Modi Has Few Good Options to Quell India’s ‘Cockroach’ Protests - Bloomberg.com
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Modi Has Few Good Options to Quell India’s ‘Cockroach’ Protests. ## **Takeaways** by Bloomberg AISubscribe. What started as a satirical online movement two months ago has turned into one of India’s biggest student protests in years, sparking scenes of violent clashes in New Delhi. And Prime Minister Narendra Modi has few good options to stop them. Launched in May by young organizers with little political experience, the Cockroach Janta Party managed to draw crowds of students, parents and professionals into the heart of India’s capital, where they jumped police barricades and faced tear gas and baton charges in an attempt to march to the parliament on Monday. They started by demanding the resignation of India’s education minister after a series of exam scandals, but frustrations quickly morphed into broader anger at Modi’s government. ranked_evidence.title: CJP's parliament march from Jantar Mantar: India's 'cockroach' protest continues a day after police crackdown - BBC
ranked_evidence.snippet: # India's 'cockroach' protest continues a day after police crackdown. Thousands have gathered again in the Indian capital Delhi a day after a police crackdown on supporters of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led movement seeking education reforms and resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Tens of thousands of young men and women had turned up for Monday's protest and tried to march on parliament, defying a police ban. Police said 118 of their personnel were also injured and 70 protesters have been detained. Police and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government have not commented on the use of sticks and tear gas against protesters. The meeting took place against the backdrop of tens of thousands of people turning up from all over the country to participate in the CJP's call to march to parliament on the opening day of the monsoon session.

ranked_evidence.title: Indian police forcibly hospitalize Cockroach Janata Party activist on hunger strike - Los Angeles Times
ranked_evidence.snippet: * Police in New Delhi forcibly moved education reform activist Sonam Wangchuk to a hospital after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike. NEW DELHI — Police forcibly transferred a prominent activist to a hospital in New Delhi on Saturday after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike tied to India’s Cockroach Janata Party movement for education reform. Delhi police said that Wangchuk was taken to the hospital after his health worsened during the hunger strike and that a brief commotion occurred when some protesters tried to block the move. The Cockroach Janata Party — a play on the name of India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party — said in a social media post that the government “forcefully abducted” Wangchuk “without his or his family’s consent” two days before their planned march to India’s Parliament.

ranked_evidence.title: What Is the Youth-Led ‘Cockroach Movement’ Staging Mass Protests in India? - Time Magazine
ranked_evidence.snippet: But it has quickly swelled into a formidable real-world political force, bringing tens of thousands of protesters into the streets in the country’s capital in recent days to call for the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and reforms to India’s troubled education system. Thousands of supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) continued to protest in the capital of New Delhi on Wednesday even after demonstrations earlier in the week erupted into violent clashes with the police that left dozens of people injured. The movement’s Monday protests in New Delhi marked one of the country’s largest anti-government gatherings in years, with an estimated 20,000 people, made up mostly of students and young people, taking to the city’s streets. Amid the massive protests, a senior government minister reportedly met with CJP representatives to hear their demands, in what was seemingly the government’s first move to hold talks with members of the movement. The following day, members of the opposition party held a protest in Parliament in support of the cockroach movement protesters.

ranked_evidence.title: Police cane supporters of India’s cockroach movement as thousands gather for march - NBC News
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Police cane supporters of India’s cockroach movement as thousands gather for march. The months-old movement and the planned protest are seen as the biggest public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his third term in office. NEW DELHI — Supporters of India’s youth-led “cockroach” movement were caned by police Monday as they sought to march on parliament in the capital, New Delhi, despite authorities denying permission for the protest. The months-old movement and the planned protest are seen as the biggest public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his third term in office, drawing millions of supporters on social media before broadening its appeal. A police decision to forcibly move hunger-striking activist Sonam Wangchuk to hospital on Saturday has galvanized the movement, with thousands of supporters arriving through the night at the protest site of Jantar Mantar in the heart of New Delhi for the march on the opening day of parliament’s monsoon session.
